On Tuesday, Google announced a new feature in the US that will allow you to launch personal apps directly through the Play Store. Google first launched the ability to vibe-code […]

articles.title: Scientists recreate a bizarre quantum effect that stops a particle cold
articles.summary: Oxford physicists have recreated a bizarre quantum effect in which a particle responds to a magnetic field without ever traveling through it. Using a hybrid quantum computer, they demonstrated how introducing a simulated magnetic flux could completely halt a particle's movement through quantum interference. The experiment brings a decades-old prediction into a new setting where matter and quantum fields influence one another.

articles.title: This new qubit could be 100 times less error-prone in superfluid quantum computer breakthrough
articles.summary: A proposed qubit made with superfluid helium could cut quantum computing error rates by around 100 times by shielding quantum information from common forms of electromagnetic noise. If experiments confirm the predictions, the technology could eventually work alongside today’s superconducting qubits or serve as a new kind of quantum memory.

articles.title: Quantum computing’s “dark horse” just proved it can go universal
articles.summary: Researchers have shown that exotic quantum particles called non-Abelian anyons can perform the full range of operations needed for universal quantum computing. Using 54 qubits on Quantinuum’s H2 processor, they combined braiding and fusion to unlock capabilities that braiding alone could not provide.

articles.title: Science Corporation implants its vision-restoring chip in its first Stargardt disease patient
articles.summary: Max Hodak, the former president and co-founder of Neuralink, detailed onstage at TechCrunch Disrupt how his company's work with PRIMA is part of its path toward a novel brain-computer interface (BCI).

articles.title: Cerebras CEO says we’re nearing a future where everyone has a personal AI assistant at home
articles.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman predicts a future where personal AI assistants become as commonplace as household appliances, running partly on local devices and partly in the cloud.

articles.title: Industrial Next wants factory robots to switch tasks in minutes, not weeks
articles.summary: Industrial Next helps manufacturers automate complex, delicate tasks that have traditionally required human labor.

articles.title: Cerebras CEO pushes back on AI doomsday warnings
articles.summary: Cerebras CEO Andrew Feldman has a message for AI leaders spreading doomsday warnings: Maybe stop talking? At TechCrunch Disrupt, he argued that the industry's focus on AI's risks is drowning out its potential benefits.

articles.title: Flox Intelligence is building AI to keep wildlife away from trains, airports, and roads
articles.summary: Flox's edge devices can identify animals and use species-specific sounds to drive them away from critical infrastructure.

articles.title: Facebook is giving users more control over their algorithm
articles.summary: Meta announced the launch of its new AI-powered feature, “Your Algorithm,” a feature it first launched on Instagram.

articles.title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
articles.summary: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.

articles.title: Pluto Security raises $42M as AI gives enterprise security teams a new headache
articles.summary: The problem with giving everyone in a company access to AI tools is that people will use them in unexpected ways. And that fact is steadily seeding fears that companies now have new, gaping security holes in their systems or, at least, will soon.

articles.title: Google opens up latest AI models to 200 European researchers
articles.summary: Google announced Wednesday that it will open up its most advanced artificial intelligence models to 200 European researchers.

articles.title: Xbox is officially embracing the chaos of AI-powered game ports
articles.summary: Retro gaming is going through a wild time at the moment, thanks to decompilations and recompilations that are letting gamers port classic titles to new devices, or merge code from two different games into a single new experience. Microsoft has witnessed skateboarding being modded into Call of Duty and Halo being played in a web […]

articles.title: Facebook will let you customize your feed algorithm using AI
articles.summary: Facebook's new "Your Algorithm" feature will let you directly add and manage topics you want to see in your feed and Facebook Reels. Meta says your recommendations "respond right away" after you make updates using the new feature by hitting "interested" or "not interested" for different topics. Your Algorithm previously launched on Instagram earlier this […]

articles.summary: Earlier this month, news broke that actress Mia Goth had filed for divorce from actor and filmmaker Shia LaBeouf. An Instagram post from the account miagoth_ - marked with a blue verified checkmark - quickly spread. The post shows Goth in a T-shirt that reads "MY EX IS MY BIGGEST FAN" in bold black letters. […]

articles.title: Epic shifts to ‘AI-accelerated development’ for upcoming Disney game
articles.summary: Epic Games plans to use AI to generate code and art for an unannounced Disney game, which is now delayed from its original March release window, according to a report from Bloomberg. The project's developers have been given an "AI-first" mandate directing them to use tools like Anthropic's Claude more to finish the game. According […]

articles.title: DLSS 5 gets toned down for its Hogwarts Legacy debut next month
articles.summary: When Nvidia originally showed off DLSS 5 earlier this year, the technology immediately got branded as gen AI for video games. To gamers, Nvidia had lost the plot. I personally couldn't get over how faces were transformed using DLSS 5. The 15-year-old student from Hogwarts Legacy suddenly looked much older, and Grace from Resident Evil […]

articles.title: AI can act exactly like a human, but we still don't think it's conscious
articles.summary: A new study reveals that people draw a surprisingly sharp line between human consciousness and artificial intelligence, even when both behave identically. Researchers found that participants considered even the most responsive AI less conscious than the least responsive human. Yet when asked about "awareness" instead, people judged humans and AI much more similarly.

articles.title: Physicists discover “astonishing” property of light that defies expectations
articles.summary: Scientists have uncovered a surprising hidden ability of light that allows it to develop spinning, twisting behavior as it travels through empty space, without special lenses, mirrors, or materials. Researchers discovered that light’s internal geometry can naturally produce left- and right-handed patterns, challenging long-standing assumptions about how light behaves. By carefully arranging a beam’s structure, scientists can control where and how these spinning patterns emerge, unlocking a new way to manipulate light.

articles.title: This light-powered AI can spot deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy
articles.summary: UCLA researchers built an AI system that uses light to analyze more than a dozen videos simultaneously, detecting deepfakes with nearly 98% accuracy. Its speed, low energy demands, and resistance to attacks could make it a powerful tool for screening the growing flood of AI-generated video.

articles.title: MIT’s tiny flying robot gets 450% faster with AI
articles.summary: A new AI control system lets MIT’s tiny flying robot move with insect-like agility, boosting its speed by about 450 percent and allowing it to pull off 10 somersaults in 11 seconds. The technology could eventually enable miniature robots to search earthquake rubble and navigate dangerous spaces that conventional drones cannot reach.

articles.title: The shape behind the Einstein problem just revealed strange new physics
articles.summary: A mathematical shape famous for covering a surface without ever repeating has revealed an unexpected ability to twist light into unusual chiral patterns. The discovery could lead to new ways of controlling light, polarization, and advanced optical devices.

articles.title: AI uncovers hidden Ozempic side effects across 400,000 Reddit posts
articles.summary: AI analysis of 400,000 Reddit posts found that users of drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro, and Zepbound reported unexpected symptoms including menstrual changes, chills, hot flashes, and fatigue. Researchers cannot say the medications caused these problems, but the patterns may reveal overlooked signals worth studying.

articles.title: Tiny nanolaser could cut computer energy use in half
articles.summary: Scientists have created an ultra-small nanolaser that could eventually allow microchips to transmit information with light instead of electricity, potentially making computers faster while cutting energy use roughly in half. Thousands of the lasers could fit on a single chip, opening possibilities for more efficient data centers, smartphones, and advanced medical sensors.

articles.title: Why AI makes computer worms harder to stop
articles.summary: Anthropic's warning that AI-powered "worms" could soon spread across smart gadgets is the latest in a series of studies showing how artificial intelligence could supercharge self-spreading malware.

articles.title: Croatia tests fully driverless robotaxi service
articles.summary: A Croatian firm that launched Europe's first commercial robotaxi service earlier this year is now testing fully driverless rides in the capital, its chief executive told AFP Tuesday.

articles.title: EU takes a page from Ireland's AI playbook
articles.summary: The EU wants to catch up in the AI race by taking a cue from Ireland—an early adopter of the technology which has rolled out the red carpet for data centers despite local backlash.

articles.title: Cyberattacks hit European supermarket chains and disrupt refrigeration systems
articles.summary: Cyberattacks disrupted European supermarket chains, affecting refrigeration systems at hundreds of stores in France and forcing a major grocer to shut down websites serving customers in Europe and the United States.

articles.title: Here's how to find the learning strategy that makes AI work for you
articles.summary: Generative AI can explain a difficult concept, solve a problem, correct a sentence or produce an answer in seconds. That creates enormous opportunities for learning.

articles.title: 'Fast Tech' fuels growing e-waste concern as millions of small, low-cost electronics flood world markets
articles.summary: With annual Black Friday and holiday shopping sprees approaching, International E-Waste Day 2026 shines a spotlight on the booming trade in "Fast Tech"—USB adapters, mini fans, LED lights, electronic toys and other small, inexpensive gadgets.

articles.title: Soft robotic fish combines high-speed swimming with 3D maneuverability
articles.summary: Researchers from the Shenyang Institute of Automation (SIA) of the Chinese Academy of Sciences have developed an electrohydraulically actuated soft robotic fish that can swim at high speeds and perform agile three-dimensional (3D) maneuvers. The soft robotic fish addresses a longstanding design challenge by combining a rigid–flexible coupled propulsion system with dynamic buoyancy regulation. This allows for fast propulsion without sacrificing maneuverability.

articles.title: Microsoft's Brad Smith calls for 'real and effective' AI safety standards
articles.summary: Microsoft President Brad Smith warned Tuesday that industry and governments must "act with urgency" to create "real and effective safety standards" to contain the risks linked to artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Less platinum, cheaper hydrogen: Ultrathin electrolyzer coatings show promise
articles.summary: Hydrogen is expected to become an important energy carrier of the future, particularly for industrial applications. But this requires climate-friendly technologies that split water into hydrogen and oxygen. One major challenge is cost: PEM water electrolysis requires components that can withstand highly corrosive conditions. Some of these components are coated with platinum.
